title: Ind-etale base change for the closed etale support right adjoint
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $g:T'\to T$ be an affine morphism (the inverse image of every affine open is affine) of Noetherian schemes, where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume $g$ is locally ind-etale: on affine opens its ring homomorphisms are filtered colimits of etale algebras of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Form the Cartesian square $Z'=Z\times_TT'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with $i':Z'\hookrightarrow T'$ and $h:Z'\to Z$. Work in bounded-below derived categories of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For any closed immersion $a:W\hookrightarrow V$ with open complement $b$, let $a^!$ denote the right derived functor of $F\mapsto a^{-1}\ker(F\to b_*b^{-1}F)$ [def-pur-etale-supported-kernel]. Write $g^*,h^*$ for exact inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $i_*,i'_* $ for closed direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$h^*i^!K\xrightarrow{\sim}i'^!g^*K\qquad(K\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)).$$
It is the adjunction mate of the closed direct-image base-change isomorphism $g^*i_*\cong i'_*h^*$: after application of $i'_*$ and this identification, its composite with the closed counit is $g^*$ of the closed counit $i_*i^!K\to K$. These comparisons are $A$-linear and commute with cohomological shifts and with composition of affine ind-etale base changes. No constructibility hypothesis on $K$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images), Tag 0A45 (lemma-cohomology-with-support-triangle), and Tag 09XQ (lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic): ind-etale base change for the closed-support right adjoint, obtained from the open-complement triangle and strict-local stalk formula. This is an agent-formulated general interface for the locality used in Travaux de Gabber, Expose XVII, Definition 1.1.1 and Definition 1.4.1.

proof.text: Use the canonical supported-kernel derived adjunctions and the finite termwise exchange c. The mate counit formula gives c∘i′_*β∘ε′=g*ε exactly. Closed direct image reflects isomorphisms on D+: on each homology sheaf this follows from ordinary full faithfulness and the exact-functor homology comparison.

Take the actual counit/unit localization triangles from the bounded below localization lemma on T and T′. Apply exact g* to the first one. The open-complement comparison supplies an invertible third component commuting with the units. Use c followed by i′_*β as the first component and the identity as the second. The counit equation supplies the first square. Transport the shifted Hom-orthogonality from the closed image along c. Triangle-morphism extension makes these prescribed components a morphism of triangles. Two-out-of-three makes its first component invertible; cancel c and reflect through i′_* to obtain invertibility of β at every object.

The ordinary unit of an arbitrary additive adjunction commutes with termwise shifts on complexes and on bounded below homotopy categories. The derivedPlus unit formula and essential surjectivity of Qh transport this property to the specified derived unit; compatibility with the counit follows by the adjunction shift theorem. Exact-localization natural-isomorphism and composition comparisons commute with shifts, as seen after the faithful D+ inclusion. Thus c and c^{-1} commute with shifts. The mate of this square under the two compatible adjunctions commutes with shifts. The generic private proofs are reused from DerivedAdjunctionCommShift and RawModuleScalarCoefficientUnshifted.

Use the inverse closed-exchange pasting and identity formulas. Apply the mates correspondence, its whiskering formula and mateEquiv_vcomp, respectively mateEquiv_unitors. Evaluate at K and cancel the ambient inverse-image composition or identity comparison. These are exactly the required β composition and identity equations.
